analyst_note: Hormuz Day 72; Naval Blockade Day 30; Project Freedom Pause Day 6 (integrity compromised); WPA Day 12 Past Statutory Deadline. The May 11 evening brief marks the sharpest single-day vibe degradation in two weeks. The week opened with a diplomatic bombshell that moved the situation backward: Iran delivered its counteroffer via the Pakistan channel late May 10, and Trump rejected it within hours — 'I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' and 'they will be laughing no longer.' Energy Secretary Wright publicly telegraphed return to military method 'in the next few days' if no deal path emerges. Iran's counteroffer was not a capitulation — it was a counter-position: end war on all fronts including Lebanon, lift OFAC sanctions on Iranian oil during a 30-day negotiating window, and end the naval blockade. Trump's rejection without a counter-counter-offer is not a negotiating signal; it is a door-slam. Simultaneously, drone attacks multiplied across the Gulf during the nominal pause: UAE intercepted two Iranian drones, a cargo ship was struck in waters Qatar condemned, and Kuwait reported hostile drones in its airspace — a pattern consistent with Iran calibrating kinetic pressure while formally maintaining the ceasefire posture. Oil markets priced the breakdown immediately: Brent surged 3.16% to $104.49, crossing $104 for the first time since early May; WTI rose 3.08% to $95.42. These are the first post-rejection price signals and they confirm the market's read: the deal track is in acute crisis. Warsh Senate floor vote occurred at 5:30 PM ET — near-certain confirmation at 54-46 — resolving the first of three triple-convergence events; Powell term expiry and Reconciliation 2.0 committee deadline both remain May 15. Oregon fire season Day 4; no red flag warning issued for PNW; no new OHA measles count. Vibe 3.

vibe.rationale: Vibe drops to 3 from 4 — the first confirmed downgrade since May 8. The triggering event is structural: Iran broke its 100+ hour silence and delivered a counteroffer via Pakistan, which would normally be constructive; but Trump's instant rejection without issuing a counter-counter-offer forecloses the deal track in a qualitatively different way than Iranian silence did. Silence preserved optionality for both sides. Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection, combined with 'they will be laughing no longer' language and Energy Secretary Wright's overt military-return timeline, signals that the Project Freedom pause is now on borrowed time. The deal track is not formally dead — no party has declared it closed, no US ultimatum with a specific deadline has been issued, and the Pakistan intermediary role has not been formally terminated — but the asymmetry is now inverted: previously, Iran's non-response was the obstacle; now, Trump's rejection without a counter has made the US the obstacle to a deal path. Drone attacks across the Gulf (UAE, Qatar, Kuwait) during the nominal pause indicate Iran is not passively waiting — it is applying distributed kinetic pressure across maritime chokepoints as a coercive signal. Brent at $104.49 (+3.16%) is the market's clear read. Three factors prevent a vibe 2: (1) Iran's counteroffer is on the table and can be met with a counter-counter-offer rather than a door-slam — the Rubio-Qatari PM meeting and Qatar's involvement leave a back-channel alive; (2) Warsh confirmation resolves one of three triple-convergence variables tonight, removing an institutional uncertainty from this week's landscape; (3) no IRGC destructive cyberattack on US infrastructure through Day 8 post-Project Freedom launch. The deal's structural logic still exists — Iran came to the table — but the path to resolution just narrowed significantly. Vibe 3: acute diplomatic breakdown, oil above $104, Gulf drone escalation, military return timeline telegraphed.

items.headline: Trump Rejects Iran Counteroffer 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE'; Energy Sec Wright Telegraphs Military Return; Deal Track in Acute Crisis; No US Counter-Counter-Offer Issued
items.summary: Iran delivered its formal response to the 14-point MOU framework via the Pakistan channel late on Sunday May 10, breaking 100+ hours of silence — and President Trump immediately rejected it. In a Truth Social post, Trump wrote 'I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' and separately stated 'they will be laughing no longer,' invoking the coercive nuclear framing of his 'one big glow' statement from Saturday. The Iranian counteroffer, transmitted through Pakistani intermediaries and confirmed by multiple outlets, contained three core demands: (1) an end to the war on all fronts, explicitly including Lebanon; (2) lifting of OFAC sanctions on Iranian oil sales during a 30-day negotiating window; (3) an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iran's proposal also emphasized negotiating the Strait of Hormuz reopening, nuclear restrictions, and comprehensive sanctions relief — framing the deal as requiring simultaneous movement on multiple tracks rather than a Hormuz-first, nuclear-later sequence. Trump's rejection was unaccompanied by a US counter-counter-offer, a narrowed framework, or a modified set of demands — leaving the Pakistan channel without a response to transmit back to Tehran. Energy Secretary Chris Wright appeared on Fox Business Monday morning and stated explicitly that if it is 'clear in the next few days that there's not a good path to a negotiated settlement, we'll go back to the military method to open the strait' — the most direct executive-branch timeline for Project Freedom resumption issued by any cabinet official. This sequence — Iran responds, Trump slams, Wright telegraphs — constitutes a qualitative shift in deal-track dynamics: the obstacle is no longer Iranian silence, it is a US posture of rejection without counter-offer. Qatar's involvement as an additional channel remains operational (Secretary of State Rubio met with the Qatari Prime Minister), and no party has formally declared the negotiations terminated. The pause nominally continues on Day 6. But the structural conditions for rapid pause termination are now in place.

negotiate Hormuz, nuclear program, sanctions relief

items.headline: Gulf Drone Escalation During Pause: UAE Intercepts 2 Iranian Drones; Qatar Condemns Cargo Ship Strike; Kuwait Reports Hostile Drones; Kinetic Pressure Distributed Across Maritime Chokepoints
items.summary: Simultaneous with Iran's counteroffer transmission and Trump's rejection, drone attacks multiplied across the Gulf during the nominal Project Freedom pause — a pattern consistent with Iran applying distributed kinetic pressure across multiple maritime and territorial vectors as a coercive negotiating signal, rather than committing to a single decisive escalation that would trigger formal pause termination. The UAE intercepted two drones originating from Iranian direction; Qatar formally condemned a drone attack that struck a cargo ship in regional waters; Kuwait reported hostile drones in its airspace. None of these incidents triggered a confirmed CENTCOM self-defense strike response as of evening May 11 — the military posture remains formally paused — but the accumulation of distributed attacks during a nominal ceasefire compounds the Wright timeline signal: Iran is not sitting still, and the US is accumulating incidents that justify resumption. The pattern mirrors the Saturday naval exchange (May 9) that the previous brief flagged as an unresolved trigger: each incident that goes unresponded to during the pause creates ambiguity about the pause's integrity, while each incident that does trigger a CENTCOM response raises the question of whether the ceasefire has ended. The three Monday incidents — UAE, Qatar, Kuwait — constitute the highest single-day drone-incident count since the pause began. CENTCOM has not issued a comprehensive public statement on Monday's incidents as of 8 PM PT.

items.headline: Brent Surges to $104.49 (+3.16%), WTI $95.42 (+3.08%) on First Monday Post-Rejection; Deal Failure Trajectory Confirmed; EIA $115 Q2 Peak Back in Frame
items.summary: Monday May 11 oil futures opened and closed sharply higher as markets priced the Iran counteroffer rejection and Gulf drone escalation in the first post-weekend trading session. Brent crude with July delivery rose 3.16% to $104.49 per barrel — crossing $104 for the first time since early May and recovering all of the May 7 'deal optimism' decline; the EIA's Q2 2026 Brent peak scenario of ~$115/barrel is now directionally in frame rather than hypothetical. WTI crude with June delivery rose 3.08% to $95.42 per barrel. The asymmetry that last week's brief flagged as the weekend's directional risk (all weekend signals were oil-price-positive) materialized: Trump's rejection, Gulf drone attacks, and Wright's military-return timeline are collectively supply-disruption-risk amplifiers with no offsetting deal-positive signal. Brent is now approximately 54% above the pre-war baseline of ~$68; WTI is approximately 40% above its pre-war baseline. National average gasoline prices remain above $4.50 per gallon (AAA) and will take 2–4 additional weeks to fully reflect today's crude move. The deal-acceptance downside oil scenario — a 15–20% crude decline over 4–6 weeks — remains structurally available but requires a US counter-counter-offer, not merely Iranian patience. Every additional day without a US counter-counter-offer reduces the probability of the downside scenario and raises the probability of the EIA $115 peak scenario.

items.headline: Triple-Convergence Week Advancing: Warsh Floor Vote 5:30 PM ET Today; Powell Expiry May 15 (4 Days); Reconciliation 2.0 Deadline May 15 (4 Days); Oil Shock Inherits New Fed Chair
items.summary: Triple-convergence week's first resolution event occurs tonight: Kevin Warsh's Senate floor vote at 5:30 PM ET, at which he is expected to be confirmed by approximately 54-46, with all 53 Senate Republicans and Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) providing the majority. The vote result — and Warsh's first statement as confirmed Fed Chair-designate — will be the second major market signal of the day after Brent's spike. Warsh inherits a monetary environment now definitively shaped by the failed deal negotiation: Brent at $104.49, WTI at $95.42, national gas above $4.50, and a war-driven inflation premium that no domestic interest rate tool can address. His first policy question as incoming chair will be whether to hold, cut, or raise — with Brent above $104, cutting to support a potentially slowing economy risks entrenching war-driven inflation; holding allows the external shock to ripple through consumer prices; raising risks tipping a war-stressed economy into recession. Warsh's first FOMC meeting is expected June 16. Jerome Powell's term as Federal Reserve Chair expires May 15 — 4 days from today — the first involuntary term expiry of a sitting Fed chair in the post-WWII era. Reconciliation 2.0: the May 15 committee submission deadline requires Senate Finance, Armed Services, and all designated committees to submit their measures to the Budget Committee in the same four days. The $72B DHS/Judiciary measure (ICE/CBP, CBO-scored May 4) has cleared committee; the remaining measures — defense, health, tax — remain outstanding.

items.headline: CISA Day 8: No Confirmed Destructive IRGC Attack; But Wright Military Timeline and Gulf Drone Escalation Raise Near-Term Cyber Retaliatory Probability; CI Fortify Remains Operative
items.summary: Eight days after Project Freedom launched (May 4), CISA has confirmed no IRGC-affiliated or Handala-attributed destructive cyberattack on US critical infrastructure. CISA AA26-097A (April 7) remains the operative advisory; no updated emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or sector-specific alert was issued Monday. CI Fortify remains operative; FINRA's financial-sector heightened threat alert and NERC's grid monitoring remain active. However, the risk calculus for IRGC cyber retaliation has materially shifted as of Monday evening: three factors now combine to raise the probability of a near-term destructive cyber operation. First, Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection eliminates the deal-progress rationale for IRGC cyber restraint — previously, Iran had a diplomatic incentive to avoid triggering escalation while negotiations were live; that incentive is now severely weakened. Second, Energy Secretary Wright's 'next few days' military-return timeline signals that Project Freedom resumption is imminent — which is historically the highest-risk trigger for IRGC retaliatory cyber action, as IRGC doctrine treats cyber operations as an asymmetric response to US conventional superiority. Third, the Gulf drone attacks (UAE, Qatar, Kuwait) on Monday demonstrate that Iran is actively executing distributed kinetic operations during the pause — a behavioral pattern consistent with an adversary running parallel escalation tracks. The sustained 8-day absence of a destructive attack remains the primary positive infrastructure signal, but the structural conditions for its continuation have deteriorated sharply since Sunday morning. CISA's warning about CyberAv3ngers targeting PLCs across Government Services, Water and Wastewater, and Energy sectors remains the operative threat vector; the Handala-Stryker (200,000 devices wiped, March 2026) and Chime Financial (April 1) operations established the operational template and willingness to strike. Any CISA emergency directive, FBI IC3 flash, or private-sector OT/ICS incident report in the next 72 hours should be treated as a priority signal.

items.headline: Oregon Fire Season Day 4: No Red Flag Warning Issued; Burn Restrictions Statewide Active; Resources Positioned; East Cascades Above-Normal Onset 21 Days Out; Federal Response Capacity Gap Unresolved
items.summary: Oregon's 2026 wildfire season is now in its fourth active day (declared May 8). No National Weather Service Portland red flag warning was issued for Monday May 11 — conditions across the PNW did not achieve the concurrent temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed thresholds required for a formal watch or warning designation on Monday. However, the structural risk environment remains unchanged: Oregon's 2025-2026 winter was tied with 1934 as the warmest on record, producing dangerously low snowpack, compressed fine-fuel curing timelines, and an early-season vulnerability window. Burn restrictions remain in effect statewide through Oregon Department of Forestry permit requirements; Portland metro and BLM Oregon-Washington burn bans remain active; Washington DNR restrictions active. Oregon wildland fire resources remain in protective pre-positioning: approximately 700 wildland firefighters and 300 fire trucks supporting 16 million protected acres, supplemented by federal and tribal responders. June 1 above-normal east Cascades fire risk onset: 21 days. The structural federal response capacity concern flagged by Oregon's congressional Democrats (filed May 7: Reps. Bonamici, Hoyle, Salinas, Blumenauer, Chavez-DeRoemer) — specifically DOGE-related eliminations of Forest Service Region 6 fire science research positions and reduced pre-positioning capability — remains unaddressed by USDA or Interior as of Monday evening. No new fire ignitions of significance were reported in Oregon or Washington Monday. National wildfire acreage burned through early May: approximately 1.85 million acres, nearly double the 10-year average for this point in the year.

items.headline: WPA Day 12: Trump Iran Rejection Without Congressional Authorization Deepens Constitutional Gap; Warsh Vote Tonight Resolves First Triple-Convergence Event; Reconciliation 4 Days to Deadline
items.summary: Today is WPA Day 12 past the April 29 statutory deadline — the deepest into unauthorized war operations the current administration has run. Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection of Iran's counteroffer, combined with Energy Secretary Wright's explicit military-return timeline, raises the probability of Project Freedom resumption in the next several days without any congressional authorization having been obtained. Should Project Freedom resume, each day of renewed offensive operations under the War Powers Resolution would add to the constitutional accountability deficit with no mechanism for congressional remedy in place: Senate Republicans have rejected six Democratic war-powers resolutions, and no seventh has been scheduled. The Trump administration's operative legal interpretation — that the WPA clock stopped when the president declared hostilities 'effectively ended' via ceasefire — remains contested but unadjudicated, having not been litigated in federal court. Tonight's Warsh floor vote (5:30 PM ET) is the first of three triple-convergence resolutions due this week: Warsh is near-certain to confirm at approximately 54-46, with all 53 Senate Republicans plus Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA). A confirmed Warsh removes one institutional uncertainty from the week but does not reduce the combined Powell expiry (May 15) and Reconciliation 2.0 deadline (May 15) pressure over the next four days. Reconciliation 2.0 status: The DHS/Judiciary $72B measure is CBO-scored and cleared; Senate Finance, Armed Services, Health, and tax-related committees must submit measures by May 15 or accept the political cost of a Trump-deadline miss. Alabama and Tennessee redistricting special sessions continue; no ACLU or NAACP Legal Defense Fund legal challenge filed; November 2026 map-lock window approximately 4.5 months and narrowing.

items.headline: PNW Fire Season Day 4: No Red Flag Warning; National Acreage Nearly Double 10-Yr Average; Resources Positioned; Federal Capacity Gap Unresolved; East Cascades Onset 21 Days
items.summary: Oregon's 2026 wildfire season (Day 4) continued without a red flag warning event on Monday May 11. No significant fire ignitions were reported in Oregon or Washington. Statewide Oregon ODF permit restrictions and Portland metro burn bans remain in effect; Washington DNR restrictions active. The national context for PNW fire season is stark: wildfires have burned approximately 1.85 million acres across the United States through early May 2026, nearly double the 10-year average for this point in the year — a figure that reflects accelerated fire behavior driven by the same drought-snowpack-heat conditions defining the PNW outlook. Oregon's 2025-2026 winter (tied warmest on record since 1934) and record-low snowpack create conditions in which the above-normal June 1 east Cascades onset is less a forecast and more a structural certainty. The 700 wildland firefighters and 300 fire trucks positioned across Oregon's 16 million protected acres represent the state's protective architecture heading into the peak window. The federal response capacity gap (Forest Service Region 6 DOGE cuts to fire science research positions and pre-positioning resources, flagged by Oregon congressional Democrats May 7) remains unaddressed as of Monday evening. AccuWeather's 2026 season projection of 5.5 million acres nationally remains operative; NIFC's above-normal outlook for the Northwest east of the Cascades from June 1 through at least August is the authoritative seasonal frame. June 1 above-normal east Cascades onset: 21 days.

The last published Oregon figure remains approximately 20 confirmed cases as of April 22, 2026, with OHA officials consistently acknowledging substantial suspected underreporting and the wastewater surveillance dashboard continuing to detect measles viral concentrations in counties with no published confirmed cases. Washington State holds at 40+ confirmed cases year-to-date across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in formal outbreak status. The school-year vaccination catch-up window has narrowed to approximately 4 weeks (PNW districts close mid-to-late June), down from 5 weeks in yesterday's brief. The structural transmission dynamics — below-threshold MMR vaccination coverage pockets, active school-year community spread, and DOGE-related CDC response constraints — remain unchanged. If the OHA count is not published Tuesday May 12, the gap between the last published figure (April 22) and the next published figure will approach 3 weeks — a significant surveillance lag given active wastewater detection. PNW pump price relief from any crude price move is now further delayed: Brent's rise to $104.49 on Monday adds a new baseline, and any consumer-level relief at the pump would take a minimum of 2–4 additional weeks from today's close.
